title: First working day and insurance start date
purpose: Ask for the first working day (the contractual start date) in step 1, without a separate step, and derive the pension fund's insurance start date from it.

stories.title: Employee confirms the first working day
stories.i_want: to enter my first working day in the first step of the onboarding questionnaire, 'About you'
stories.so_that: the pension fund and HR use the start date I actually agreed on, including when it moved after I signed my contract
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day 'the number one thing' for the pension fund, and it often moves (F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-e3721e). Without it the fund registration is blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is asked of and required from every employee in step 1
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they complete step 1 'About you' (first name, last name, date of birth, first working day)
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is asked of and required from every employee, whatever their residence, nationality or civil status. It is part of step 1, and the questionnaire has no separate step for it. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the eight-step order in D-047.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is the contractual start date
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose contractual start date falls on a weekend or a public holiday
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: they enter the contractual start date as is, and it is accepted even on a weekend or public holiday. The questionnaire explains that the contractual start date is meant. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the first working day is the contractual start date (D-039).

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed form and range of the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee enters their first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is a calendar date written as DD.MM.YYYY. It must lie within one year after the questionnaire was sent; if it does not, the employee is told the date is not accepted and cannot continue until they correct it. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the one-year limit comes from D-050.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is recorded for the pension fund, as the basis of the insurance start date, and for HR, which plans the start and keeps the fund registration up to date. The employee is not asked for the insurance start date.

acceptance_criteria.title: Only HR changes the first working day after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire and their start date later moves
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee wants to change the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee cannot change it in the questionnaire, which is read-only after submission. Only HR can change the date; how HR does this is specified in the later HR-side spec. The latest date always counts, and no history of earlier dates is kept.

stories.title: Derive the pension insurance start date from the first working day
stories.i_want: to receive an insurance start date on the 1st of a month, derived from the employee's first working day
stories.so_that: the registration's required 'Insurance start date' is valid without the employee having to know or work out the fund's rule
stories.priority_reason: The 'Insurance start date' is a required field of the fund registration and must be the 1st of a month (F-pension_portal-509cbe, F-pension_portal-dd8126). A wrong date led to an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66).

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date is derived, never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are never asked for the insurance start date. Lonio derives it from the first working day and records it for the pension fund as a date in the format DD.MM.YYYY that is always the 1st of a month.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the first working day itself. This also applies when that day is a weekend or public holiday, because the first working day is the contractual start date. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: see D-039.

examples.name: Start on the 1st of a month
Contractual start on a Saturday and Swiss National Day

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on any other day
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is not the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the 1st of the following month, including across a year end.

examples.name: Julia (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-e18e66), start moved to 15 March (year assumed)
Start on the 2nd of a month
Start at the end of the year

stories.title: Re-derive the insurance start date when the first working day moves
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived again every time the first working day changes
stories.so_that: the date at the pension fund never drifts from the actual start date, as it did for Julia
stories.priority_reason: A missed update after Julia's start date moved caused a wrong date at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66). Start dates move often (F-hr_transcript-e3721e).

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date always follows the latest first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day was changed, either by the employee before submission or by HR after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: it is derived from the latest first working day only. Earlier dates and the insurance start dates derived from them are not kept. How the changed date reaches the pension fund belongs to the separate transmission and HR-side topics.
